question.text: Ms. Anjali Kapoor, a resident individual LP, receives pass-through LTCG of INR 10 lakh from Neelkanth Listed Equity Alpha Fund (Cat II AIF, STT paid on both sides of the fund's trades). She has no other LTCG in FY25. Under Section 112A, what is her tax liability (basic rate, ignore surcharge/cess)?

answer.text: INR 1,09,375 (12.5% of INR 8.75 lakh after INR 1.25 lakh exemption)

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 112A (post FY25): LTCG on STT-paid listed equity shares is exempt up to INR 1,25,000 per FY (raised from INR 1 lakh by Finance (No.2) Act 2024 w.e.f. 23-07-2024). Excess taxable at 12.5% without indexation. Taxable = 10,00,000 - 1,25,000 = 8,75,000. Tax = 12.5% x 8,75,000 = INR 1,09,375. The Trap: Option B forgets the exemption. Option C uses the pre-23-07-2024 rate (10%). Option D cites Section 10(38) which was withdrawn from 1 April 2018. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III) frames this at fund level; XIX-C expects LP-level computation for Form 64C disclosure. Manager's Pro-Tip: In the LP's Form 64C, disclose gross LTCG — do NOT net the INR 1.25 lakh at fund level. Exemption is LP-specific and must be claimed in the LP's ITR where they have aggregate LTCG visibility.
